name: Prepare the monthly cost report and forecast
summary: Every month each project produces a cost report that compares budget, committed cost and cost to date by cost code and forecasts the cost to complete and the final margin. The project accountant cleans job cost, project controls builds the report, the superintendent measures self-performed work, the project manager forecasts each code and the operations manager and finance review it. The forecast sets percent complete and therefore revenue, so optimistic estimates show up later as write-downs; the work is squeezed between the AP cut-off and the corporate close.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 220 active building projects, an ERP job cost ledger, Excel cost report workbooks and monthly job reviews by regional operations managers.
baseline.notes: Revenue is recognised over time on a cost-to-cost basis, so the forecast feeds the monthly and quarterly close. COVID-19 productivity losses in 2020-2021 and material escalation in 2021-2022 made forecasts move more than in an ordinary year.

unit_of_work: one project cost report for one month
trigger: Finance issues the preliminary job cost report after the AP and payroll cut-off, a few working days after month end.
end_state: The forecast is approved, locked in the ERP for revenue recognition and published to the regional cost report.

volume.seasonality: One report per active project every month; quarter-end months (March, June, September, December) get closer review because they feed published results.

evidence.note: One report per active project; 220 active projects from the organisation file.

systems.name: Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)
AP invoice scanning and approval workflow
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Field time capture (paper sheets or tablet app keyed to cost codes)
Equipment management (fleet register, rates, maintenance work orders)
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)

steps.name: Review job cost detail for miscodings
steps.description: The project accountant opens the preliminary job cost report for the project after the AP and payroll cut-off, scans the transactions posted this month by cost code, and recodes invoices, timesheets and equipment charges that landed on the wrong code or the wrong job.

error.defect_description: A miscoding is missed and stays in the wrong cost code.

evidence.note: Bills must be processed through job costing before the month is closed; review time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Accrue unbilled subtrade and material cost
steps.description: The project accountant compares the trade progress billings and material receipts for the month with the invoices posted, and books accruals for work done but not yet invoiced so the cost to date reflects the work in place.

error.defect_description: Accrual missed or doubled when the invoice arrives.

control.basis: Period-end cut-off of job costs for IFRS 15 cost-to-cost revenue recognition (TSX-listed issuer)

evidence.note: Cost-to-cost percent complete depends on complete costs to date.

steps.name: Build the cost report workbook
steps.description: The project controls specialist exports budget, approved changes, commitments and costs to date by cost code from the ERP into the company's monthly cost report workbook, rolling forward last month's forecast so each line shows its prior estimate.

error.defect_description: Export misses a cost code or a new commitment.

evidence.note: Excel cost report fed from the ERP was the common tool in 2019-2022; each specialist covers about nine projects.

steps.name: Reconcile commitments and pending changes
steps.description: The project controls specialist checks open subcontract and purchase order balances against the commitment register, adds subcontract change orders and backcharges agreed but not yet issued, and lists exposures where trades have priced extras.

error.defect_description: A trade extra that has been priced but not issued is left out.

evidence.note: Share of projects with self-performed concrete or carpentry is the author's estimate from the organisation's self-perform crews.

steps.name: Compare self-perform labour and equipment with budget
steps.description: The project controls specialist pulls this month's crew hours from timekeeping and equipment charges by cost code, divides by installed quantities to get unit rates, and flags codes where productivity is below the estimate.

error.defect_description: Hours coded to the wrong activity distort the unit rate.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common self-perform cost control.

steps.name: Measure installed quantities and remaining crew hours
steps.description: The superintendent walks the self-perform work with the drawings, measures formwork placed, concrete poured and carpentry installed to date, and estimates the crew hours and equipment weeks still needed, correcting any hours booked to the wrong code.

error.defect_description: Remaining hours underestimated, usually by assuming productivity will recover.

control.basis: Site orientation, PPE and fall protection for persons walking an active site (Ontario O. Reg. 213/91)

evidence.note: Superintendent input on self-perform quantities is common practice; the organisation file does not list the superintendent on this process.

steps.name: Forecast cost to complete by cost code
steps.description: The project manager works down every cost code, comparing budget, committed cost and cost to date, and types an estimate to complete for each, deciding where buyout savings are real and where overruns will continue to the end of the job.

error.defect_description: Optimistic estimate to complete that hides a fade (overrun deferred in hope of recovery).

evidence.note: The PM owns cost to complete; delaying recognition of overruns is a common error. Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide which change revenue to include
steps.description: The project manager reviews the change order log, includes signed change orders in contract value, judges which pending quotations and directives are probable enough to forecast, and matches each with its forecast cost so margin is not overstated.

error.defect_description: Unapproved change revenue forecast without its cost or before it is probable.

evidence.note: Change order log with status and ageing is part of the monthly job review packet.

steps.name: Forecast general conditions and schedule costs
steps.description: The project manager checks the schedule's forecast completion date, extends site staff, trailers, cranes, hoarding and winter heat to that date, and adds the cost of any delay or acceleration not yet covered by a change.

error.defect_description: Forecast assumes the original finish date although the schedule has slipped.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter the forecast and compute margin
steps.description: The project controls specialist enters the cost-to-complete figures in the ERP forecast screen or cost report, and the workbook computes forecast final cost, margin, percent complete on a cost-to-cost basis and the over- or under-billed position.

error.defect_description: Keying error in a large code.

evidence.note: Cost-to-cost percent complete and over/under billing.

steps.name: Check the forecast for anomalies
steps.description: The project controls specialist looks for negative costs to complete, codes over budget with no forecast change, percent complete far from schedule progress and swings from last month, and sends questions back to the project manager.

evidence.note: Share returned is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the forecast narrative
steps.description: The project manager writes a short narrative for the cost report: what moved the margin since last month, the main risks and opportunities, pending changes, and the billing position and actions to recover any underbilling.

evidence.note: Review outputs include the 1-3 factors driving margin and billing actions.

steps.name: Review the forecast in the monthly job review
steps.description: The operations manager meets the project manager and project controls specialist, goes through the cost report line by line against the original bid margin and last month, challenges optimistic estimates to complete, and approves or sends it back.

next.condition: approved but margin fade above threshold or loss job

evidence.note: Monthly review compares current margin with prior months and the original bid. Shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Regional vice-president reviews a fading job
steps.description: For a job whose margin has faded beyond the reporting threshold or is forecast to lose money, the regional vice-president reviews the cost report with the operations manager, sets a recovery plan and approves the reduced forecast for reporting.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: margin fade above threshold escalated to regional executive

evidence.note: Escalation threshold practice is the author's estimate; the regional VP is not listed on this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Finance reviews the forecast against the WIP
steps.description: The regional finance manager compares the approved forecast with the work-in-progress schedule, revenue recognised to date and billings, questions unusual margin swings and unapproved change revenue, and decides whether a loss provision is needed.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: finance review of contract estimates (NI 52-109 certification)

evidence.note: Controllers read the WIP monthly; sureties and banks also review it. Shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Calculate the loss provision
steps.description: The financial reporting analyst calculates the full expected loss on the contract from the forecast, documents the estimate for the auditors, and prepares the provision entry so the whole loss is recognised this period rather than spread over the job.

control.basis: IFRS (IAS 37 onerous contracts / IFRS 15) applied by TSX-listed issuers

evidence.note: Accounting standard requirement from the author's general knowledge; the analyst is not listed on this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Lock the forecast and pass it to the close
steps.description: The project accountant locks the forecast version in the ERP, posts the percent complete used for revenue recognition and the over- or under-billing adjustment, and confirms to the corporate close team that the project is final.

control.basis: IFRS 15 input method requires the period-end estimate of total contract cost

steps.name: Publish the cost report to dashboards
steps.description: The overnight reporting job refreshes the regional cost report and margin dashboards from the locked forecasts and distributes them to the operations review and owner meeting packs without anyone touching it.

evidence.note: Overnight refresh of Excel or Power BI reports is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Forecast sent back at the job review
exceptions.description: The operations manager challenges the cost to complete and the PM re-forecasts the affected codes.

exceptions.name: Margin fade escalated
exceptions.description: Fade beyond threshold or a loss job goes to the regional vice-president for a recovery plan.

exceptions.name: Loss provision
exceptions.description: A forecast loss is provided for in full this period.

exceptions.name: Fully subcontracted project
exceptions.description: No self-perform labour or equipment to measure, so the superintendent step is skipped.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the preliminary job cost report to the published forecast
benchmarks.population: Monthly project cost reports at Canadian general contractors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: forecasts due to finance around the 8th to 12th working day after month end so the close can finish within about three weeks.

benchmarks.unit: percentage points of margin lost between bid (20%) and current forecast (14%)
benchmarks.population: Illustrative example in a CFMA practitioner post

evidence.note: An example, not a population statistic.

pain_points.description: Project managers defer recognising overruns, expecting to recover them, so fades appear late and in large steps.
Costs to date lag the field because invoices and accruals are late, so the forecast is built on stale numbers.

evidence.note: Stale or manually reconciled data trails the field.

pain_points.description: Re-keying between ERP exports and the Excel cost report, and back into the ERP, adds errors and checking time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 tooling.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (1.35 loading on salaried wages).

The superintendent, regional vice-president and financial reporting analyst are included because measuring self-performed work, approving fades and booking loss provisions need them; the organisation file lists only the PM, project controls, operations manager and project accountant on this process.
Equipment charges and the schedule are added as standing inputs; the organisation file lists them for other processes only.
The project manager's forecasting time (about 8 hours per project per month including rework) is the author's estimate; it equals about 13.5 FTE, or 12% of the 110 project managers' time.
Revenue recognition entries themselves are posted in fin-month-end-close; this workflow ends when the forecast is locked.
Simulated median cycle time is 10.2 days (p90 14.8) against the 9-day estimate; the extra day comes from forecasts sent back for revision. Stated FTEs (32.4) match touch time x volume.

sources.supports: Percent complete on a cost-to-cost basis (cost incurred / total estimated cost); earned revenue and over- or under-billing; margin fade example of 20% bid margin falling to 14%; controller reads the WIP monthly so the PM can act; sureties and banks review WIP for fade across the backlog.

sources.title: Cost to Complete: An Essential Monthly Metric
sources.publisher: Journal of Light Construction, Ian Schwandt
sources.supports: The project manager owns cost to complete; accounting processes bills and produces the WIP; the month is not closed until bills are job-costed, cost to complete is updated and production agrees; delaying recognition of cost overruns in the hope of recovering them distorts the WIP and revenue.

sources.title: The Monthly Job Review: The Operating System Behind Predictable Profit for Contractors
sources.supports: Monthly job review with numbers updated before the meeting; packet of summary sheet, contract extract, job cost review with forecast support and change order log; outputs are an updated forecast, billing actions and follow-ups; underbilling and billing lagging production as problems the review catches.
